author: Ian Fenty <ifenty@users.noreply.github.com>
commit message:
Adjointable Sea Ice Thermodynamics: part deux (#242)

* Preliminary files required for the new seaice adjoint codes:

Includes
1. adding seaice_growth_adx.F, seaice_solve4temp_adx.F to seaice_ad_diff.list
2. adding calls to seaice_growth_adx.F in seaice_model.F
3. adding new seaice parameters to SEAICE_PARAMS.h and SEAICE_readparms.
4. adding new adjoint/forward run dependent seaice parameters to autodiff files

* First version of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F + seaice_solve4temp_adx.F codes

These two codes, seaice_growth_adx.F (formerly seaice_growth_if.F) and
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F (formerly seaice_budget_ice.F) date from spring
2010.  They were used for the state estimation work in the Fenty 2010
Ph.D. thesis and the Fenty and Heimbach 2012a paper.

The '_adx' suffix is chosen to indicate that these routines are useful for adjoint calculations.

Note: these two codes (and up to 5th version) will not run 'as-is'  they are included here to
be part of the seaice_growth_adx.F evolution record.

* Second version of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F + seaice_solve4temp_adx.F codes

These two codes, seaice_growth_adx.F (formerly seaice_growth_if.F) and
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F (formerly seaice_budget_ice.F) date from Summer
2010.  They were used for experiments showing the importance of positive
surface buoyancy forcing from melting sea ice that is advected south
over the Labrador Sea in Fenty 2010 Thesis and the Fenty and Heimbach 2012b paper.

* Third set of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F + seaice_solve4temp_adx.F codes

These two codes, seaice_growth_adx.F (formerly seaice_growth_if.F) and
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F (formerly seaice_budget_ice.F) date from winter
2010/2011 and were created to integrate the Fenty sea ice codes with the
MITgcm main branch.  MIT folks decided to rewrite the seaice_growth.F
instead and so from then on the Fenty seaice growth codes lived quiet
and peaceful lives in the MITgcm contrib directory
/MITgcm_contrib/ifenty/Fenty_seaice_thermo_code_merge/code_update

* Fourth set of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F + seaice_solve4temp_adx.F
codes

These two codes, seaice_growth_adx.F (formerly seaice_growth_if.F) and
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F (formerly seaice_budget_ice.F) date from Jan 2013.
Codes taken from
MITgcm_contrib/ifenty/Fenty_Thermo_Code_Updates/code_updates_20130122/

* Fifth version of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F + seaice_solve4temp_adx.F codes

These two codes, seaice_growth_adx.F (formerly seaice_growth_if.F) and
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F (formerly seaice_budget_ice.F) date from early 2015.

They were not stored in /contrib but from a personal subversion repository 
of Fenty.  They appear to be the first of the 'reborn' versions.

Codes taken from /Users/ifenty/Work/poise/ModelConfigurations/branches/MergingMyIceGrowthCodeToCurrentMITgcm/SeaIceGrowthReborn

Note: these two codes (and earlier version) will not run 'as-is'  they are included here to
be part of the seaice_growth_adx.F evolution record.

* Sixth version of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F code

This seaice_growth_adx.F (formerly seaice_growth_if.F) is from sometime after early 2015.

Apparently this version of the Fenty seaice_growth code was the starting
point for  Arash Bigdeli.  The seaice_solve4temp_adx.F code is
structually the same as version 5.  Here the subroutine name is changed
in the file to seaice_solve4temp_adx.F and the TAF store calls use
seaice_solve4temp_adx instead of seaice_solve4temp.

Codes from
MITgcm_contrib/ifenty/Fenty_seaice_thermo_code_merge/reborn_c65h/code/seaice_growth.F

Note: these two codes (and later version) will run 'as-is'.
To invoke them, add the following line to  SEAICE_OPTIONS.h :

They were used to validate that the changes made by Bigdeli (version
seven) did not change the adjoint gradients in the 1D thermodynamic
verification experiment's 11000 time step test.

* Seventh version of adjointable seaice_growth_adx.F and
seaice_solve4temp_adx.F codes.

This version of seaice_growth_adx.F builds on version six.  It includes
Arash Bigdeli's improvements for properly handling freshwater fluxes
when the model is configured with a nonlinear free surface in
seaice_growth_adx.F, including the cases when negative values of heff
are passed to seaice_growth_adx.F after seaice advection.  There are
also new diagnostic terms to allow offline budget closure.  Salt plume
codes that had been removed in version six are added back in here.

This version of the code was compared against version six and had
identical gradients in the 1D_ocean_ice_column verification experiment
11000 time step test without salt plume defined.

* seaice_model.F: define bi,bj,i,j without TAMC
  the addition of a sea ice load calculation in seaice_growth requires
  bi,bj,i, and j which were previously required only when TAMC was defined.
  Now these counters are always defined.

* Cleaning:
- remove tabs, trailing blank, and double consecutive blank lines
- remove CVS Header and Name in seaice_solve4temp_adx.F

* remove storage directive for heffm:
  Martin removed all storage directives of HEFFM as part of PR #174
  since they are no longer needed. Curiously, these 2 (added back)
  storage dir trigger an additional TAF recomputation warning in experiment
  global_ocean.cs32x15 and offline_exf_seaice ; decide to remove/clean this
  with no impact on model results.

* Update SEAICE_OPTIONS.h
  Add a CPP option for turning on the adjointable sea ice thermodynamic output.  

The new SEAICE_OPTIONS.h now has an #undef placeholder fo rthe new CPP option
#undef ALLOW_SEAICE_GROWTH_ADX

* Remove trailing blanks
* document addition of adjointable seaice thermo.

commit message:
replace hardwired local filename length 80 by MAX_LEN_FNAM (#715)

* replace hardwired length 80 by MAX_LEN_FNAM for local filenames

- first attempt, mostly by appling these sed commands locally:
sed -i.bak 's/(80)/(MAX_LEN_FNAM)/g' *.F
sed -i.bak 's/( 80)/(MAX_LEN_FNAM)/g' *.F
sed -i.bak 's/(80a)/(a)/g' *.F
sed -i.bak 's/(1:80)//g' *.F
with some fine tuning "by hand". I excluded all diagnostics related
declarations (diagTitle etc.), local filenames (e.g. pickups) for
which it is safe to use 80 characters, unclear usage (e.g. in fizhi),
pkg/admtlm (altogether), and pkg/atm_ocn_coupler (because none of the
files include EEPARAMS.h where MAX_LEN_FNAM is defined).

* remove (most) unnecessary initialisations of local fname

* put back modified if block

- it would be good to add a proper emergency stop here.

* replace MAX_LEN_MBUF by MAX_LEN_FNAM for consistent initialisation

* further simplify

* minor: upper/lower case changes

* Document file-name declaration update

commit message:
Re-wrote the convective mixing algorithm to use pre-calculated weights.

Uses two new routines:
 - convective_weights() calculates mixing factors A and B, called once
 - convectively_mixtracers() mixes a tracer (argument) using A and B
   and is called for each tracer

The old call to convect() is simply commented out for the time-being.
Similarly, convect.F still exists. I thought it prudent to leave them
around until the TAF/TAMC related bits are added.

author: Gael Forget <gforget@mit.edu>
commit message:
- switch to HO = 0.2
  To be better consistent with thsice and initial condition.
  With SEAICE_areaLossFormula = 1, HO has a large influence on
  the ~ equilibrium solution. The three terms of melt/growth
  act separately on ice concentration, which stays below 1.
- switch to SEAICE_areaLossFormula = 2
  Leads to a ~ equilibrium solution (after 3 years run)
  that is ~1 for ice concentration (in cold atm sector)
  similar to the thsice solution.
- switch to SEAICE_growMeltByConv = .TRUE.
  Has little influence with SEAICE_areaLossFormula = 2
- switch to SEAICE_doOpenWaterMelt = .TRUE.
  Has little influence with SEAICE_areaLossFormula = 2
  over most of the domain. But there were spurious 500m ice
  in the extreme cold part of the domain (top right corner,
  where the ocean is below freezing) that are
  removed when using SEAICE_doOpenWaterMelt.
- these parameter choices do not seem to affect
  the adjoint accuracy much.

commit message:
Small ecco cleaning (#549)

* small changes for more robust results

- change "facNum" expression to be consistent with comment in src code:
  "facNum is 1 divided by the number of tiles in SIZE dot h"
  by adding number of tile in X per proc (i.e., nSx);
- also change "facNum" from a parameter to just a local var (some compiler do not
  accept division in parameter definition) and compute it in double precision.
- similar double precision change for "facCost"
- small cleaning: remove copies itlo,ithi,jtlo,jthi ; identation ; remove wrong
  S/R name in S/R description ; few lower/upper case changes.

* fix SEAICECOST_JPL code

- fix few calls in SEAICECOST_JPL code where gencost_weight is passed
  as argument to S/R ECCO_READWEI & ECCO_CP

* minor adjustment for TLM

Remove "costfinal" file before running TLM in dir that might be used to run Divided-Adjoint.
This is just in case a user run a TLM testreport without cleaning the run-dir where
a Divided-Adjoint was run before (e.g., in lab_sea/run/).

* fix missing initialisation of "active_var"

- halo region of argument variable "active_var" were not initialised
  (but used later on in this S/R); fix by calling ECCO_ZERO.
- also simplify computation of "recip_nyearsRL" (now use single conversion)
  to be more robust in getting double precision results.

* document fixing minor issues in pkg/ecco

author: Jean-Michel Campin <jmc@ocean.mit.edu>
commit message:
Fix AB time-stepping of QuasiHydrostatic with staggerTimeStep

1) add "myTime" and "myIter" arguments to S/R MOM_QUASIHYDROSTATIC and update
  S/R calls in calc_phi_hyd.F ;
2) re-arrange mom_quasihydrostatic.F : use local array (gWinBuoy) to collects various
  (currently 2, Coriolis and NH-metric terms) contributions of quasi-hydrostatic vertical
  acceleration ; And at the end, convert vertical acceleration and add to Buoyancy argument.
  This does affect results at machine truncation level.
3) for Stagger time-step, since (Quasi) Hydrostatic pressure gradient is kept
  outside AB time-stepping (as it should for pure buoyancy contribution), needs
  to apply AB to quasi-hydro contributions (AB was previously missing here):
  Apply Adams-Bashforth extrapolation to local array gWinBuoy ; implemented
  both for AB-2 and AB-3.

author: Martin Losch <Martin.Losch@awi.de>
commit message:
o OBCS and PTRACERS: add open boundary support for passive tracers
  - either use homogenous (pseudo) v.Neumann conditions or prescribe
    OB-values from file; this is not different from the way theta and salinity
    are treated
  - however, Orlanski-radiation conditions are not supported, and the model
    will stop if you use pTracers and Orlanski at the same time.
  - beefed up the rountine obcs_external_fields_load: now only those open
    boundary values are overwritten with values from files for which there
    are really files, otherwise the OB-fields remain untouched. This makes
    it possible to use different OBs at different ends of the domain (as
    with EXF)
  - TODO: add support for OB?w and OB?eta, which can currently not be read
    from a file.

commit message:
Update optfile for gfortran v10

- with recent version of gfortran (version 10.*), need to have special option
  "-fallow-argument-mismatch" to avoid stopping when compiling src files that
  contain multiple routine calls with 1 argument beeing of different type between
  calls (in this case, the type of argument depends on value of an other argument).
  This is very common with MPI subroutine calls and difficult to avoid when most
  of S/R are in the same file (e.g., ad_taf_output.f).
- Try to get the compiler version leading number and only add option above
  for compiler version 10 or higher.

author: Torge Martin <torge.martin@gmail.com>
commit message:
Introducing a new parameterization for grease ice,
 i.e. newly formed sea ice in open water:

What it does:
 The grease ice parameterization delays formation of solid
 sea ice from frazil ice by a time constant and provides a
 dynamic calculation of the initial solid sea ice thickness
 HO as a function of winds, currents and available grease ice
 volume. Grease ice does not significantly reduce heat loss
 from the ocean in winter and area covered by grease is thus
 handled like open water.
 (for details see Smedsrud and Martin, 2014, Ann.Glac.)

How to use:
- enable SEAICE_GREASE in SEAICE_OPTIONS.h
- set SItrName(1) = 'grease' in namelist SEAICE_PARM03 in data.seaice
  then output SItr01 is SItrNameLong(1) = 'grease ice volume fraction',
  with SItrUnit(1) = '[0-1]', which needs to be multiplied by SIheff
  to yield grease ice volume.
- additionally, the actual grease ice layer thickness
  (diagnostic SIgrsLT) can be saved.

This method is based on tagging grid-cell center according to latitude position
relative to target-latitude vector "yLat"; and then collecting the interface

with a jump in tag value across the corresponding latitude target.

  allow to restart (but not perfect restart) if field is missing in pickup.

  storage arrays ; stop if trying to use QuasiHydrostatic with staggerTimeStep
  while this new option is not defined.

commit message:
Major refactoring and bugfixes for data preprocessed by nnUNet

Refactoring:
- move steps to generate a single pair to a separate function, generate_single_pair and update generate_pair.
- rename data_augmentation to random_flip_all_axes and update generate_pair.
- added documentation about expected inputs and outputs

Bugfixes for data preprocessed by nnUNet:
- change axes of random_flip_all_axes from [0, 1, 2] to [-1, -2, -3] to allow any number of preceding dimensions (e.g., multiple MRI modalities)
- change points in nonlinear_transformation to allow z-score normalisation (instead of [0, 1] range)
- apply local_pixel_shuffling to all modalities instead of the first only
- update image_in_painting  and image_out_painting to work with a single modality, allowing per-modality in & out painting

commit message:
a bug on softamx and K.set_image_data_format("channels_first")

Hi Zhou, 

We have been trying your amazing code for days, thanks for your work!

We found a bug on your README on how to use your pretrained model for segmentation.

Your model code define a channel-first implementation
```python
K.set_image_data_format("channels_first")
```
, where inputs: `B x C x D x H x W`. Thereby, your output `final_convolution` is also `B x C x D x H x W`.

If you run.
```python
output = Activation('softmax')(final_convolution)
```
The default `softmax` is compute the normalized term on the `axis=-1`, i.e. the `W`-axis, which is usually not what people want.
